text:
alex: PR opened with tenant-tagging examples + autoscale narrative for the Dedicated docs. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/6789 -- want quick eyes before I land.

maria: taking a look now. quick summary of changes? is this mostly examples or wording changes too? :eyes:

alex: mostly examples (tenant labels, reservation examples), plus a new short section that narrates how autoscale decisions are made (cooldown, burst vs reserved). also a tiny copy change to the SLA paragraph — see line 72.

sophie: re SLA wording — can we avoid ambiguous phrases like "best-effort fallback"? legal flagged that when we used it last time. propose: use "best-effort fallback (no SLA)" or add an explicit sentence about conditions.

andre: +1 on clarifying. also the isolation example needs a concrete annotation for tenant labels. right now examples are vague. e.g. show `isolation: tenant_tag` and ``preemption_policy: best-effort`` in the snippet.

alex: good call. added a new python SDK snippet in the PR showing `tenant_label` usage. preview below:

```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient()
res = client.create_reservation(
    name="analytics-reservation",
    gpu_type="A100",
    capacity=8,
    tenant_label={"team": "recommendations"},
    isolation="tenant_tag"
)
print(res.id)
```

maria: yeah that helps. can you add a second snippet showing a fallback policy? e.g. how to route to cheaper quantized model when reserved capacity is saturated.

alex: added a JSON routing policy example and a curl sample in the PR description.

andre: small nit: the examples reference an internal link /handbook/dedicated/legacy that 404s in the preview. please fix links to point to the new handbook path.

dev-docs-bot: deploy preview built: https://deploy-preview-6789--docs.redwood.ai (generated at 2026-03-22T18:02:11Z) :white_check_mark:

sophie: I checked the preview. isolation example renders but the YAML block is missing the `preemption_policy` field because of a markdown escaping issue. looks like a triple backtick fence followed by indentation caused the parser to drop a leading space.

alex: thanks. will fix the fence. also tagging @maria for SLA phrasing — changed to: "In the event of capacity constraints, Redwood may automatically reroute requests to compatible model variants. Such reroutes are not covered by SLA unless explicitly stated in the customer contract." thoughts?

maria: that language is good. maybe add a single example scenario bullet: "If Dedicated pool is completely saturated for >2m, traffic may be routed to hosted quantized variant; customer notified via console + alerting."

andre: please also add a one-line migration note for teams using older tenant label key `owner` -> `team` to avoid mismatches when we enforce label normalization in the next release.

alex: added migration note and a tiny script to remap labels in the migration guide. snippet: 

```bash
# remap owner->team for reservations
redwood-cli reservations list --filter owner:* \
  | jq '.[] | .labels.team = .labels.owner | del(.labels.owner)' \
  | xargs -I{} redwood-cli reservations update {}
```

sophie: nice. one more ask: can we add a short paragraph under the autoscale narrative explaining tradeoffs of longer cooldowns vs latency spikes? product wants that for PMs.

alex: done — two bullets added. left a TODO for graphs later.

maria: LGTM from docs side. leaving final technical accuracy to eng-pt.

andre: approved, but please fix the 404 link and the YAML fence before merge.

alex: fixed both. merging tomorrow morning unless anyone objects. thanks all :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — can we also add a quick note in the release notes about the label normalization? ops will need to run a check.

alex: noted, adding a release-note blurb.

dev-docs-bot: PR merged by alex into main (commit 9f4b2c) — deploy queued.

alex: closing thread — followups tracked in the release notes and the migration checklist file.
